Fix the command center UI findings in docs/audits/2026-10-16-hr-assistant/command-center-ux.md, in priority order, with plain-English copy (the user is a busy non-technical HR manager):
1 (blocker) Applicant review: gui/executive.js sends applicant_id (around lines 186, 212) but the server requires applicant_ref; the panel reads review.fields/review.decisions but the server returns flat keys plus available_decisions; the list reads 'suggestion' but data has 'recommendation'. Fix all three; show score, recommendation, summary, strengths, concerns; build decision buttons from available_decisions; label 'AI suggestion - you decide'. Check the real response shape in src/agent_os/executive/window/actions_applicant_decisions.py and providers_applicants.py.
2 Confirm card: human title like 'Decline <name> (<county>)?', one-sentence consequence instead of raw JSON (keep a collapsible 'Details'), buttons named for the action / 'Keep as is', success message naming what happened, role=alertdialog and focus the primary button; must not cover the chat input.
3 Don't show 'Update county openings' on every item (only on applicant/county items); Dismiss and Snooze must call /api/act directly instead of going through the chat model.
4 Errors: red dismissible banner with Retry for provider load errors, friendly chat error styling, clear stale errors on next success; no raw exception text by default (put it under Details); never the word 'provider'.

8 Busy state 'Working on it... this can take up to a minute' near the input; chat bubbles must not stretch (align-content:start).
9 Rescue: hide the empty list when one item is shown.
10 a11y: label the chat input, role=tablist/tab with arrow keys, the warning icon needs text '(asks before doing)', preview title colour #8a5a12.
Update tests in tests/test_executive_window_gui*.py (they assert on JS/HTML text) to match.

Let the user run ALL agentic coding from the Executive command center through the Orchestrator, so every coding task gets the orchestrator's routing, budgets, review and records.
1. New src/agent_os/executive/window/actions_coding.py registering action 'coding.start' (consequential: it spends model usage). Params: goal (str), repo (registered project id from agent_os.registry canonical projects, or a path), optional project. Preview (no side effects): resolved repo/project, the goal, and the orchestrator's provider picks and cost estimate if cheaply available (agent_os.orchestrator.service.providers / quote; skip if unavailable), plus the sentence 'Starts an orchestrator run that plans, codes, tests and reviews on its own branch; nothing is merged without you.' On confirm: call agent_os.orchestrator.service.start_recommended(goal, repo, project, policy={}) WITHOUT driving it in the request thread (start it in a background thread or use the service's non-blocking path such as no-drive then a daemon thread calling engine().run_loop), and return run_id.
2. providers_orchestrator.py: in addition to gates and parked nodes, emit one 'coding_run' item per non-terminal run (title = the run goal shortened, why = state and progress like '3 of 5 tasks done', tab 'work'), and a completed-run item that stays until dismissed showing the result branch. Add actions on coding_run items: 'coding.pause', 'coding.resume', 'coding.stop' (stop is consequential) calling service.control.
3. server.py /api/chat: detect 'start a coding task: <goal>', 'code: <goal> in <repo>', 'have the orchestrator <goal>' and return a confirm preview for coding.start (never start without Confirm). Add POST /api/coding/start doing the same.
4. gui/executive.js: coding_run items show progress and Pause/Resume/Stop; the 'Start a coding task' chip prefills 'Start a coding task: '.
5. Register in builtin.py and update tests/test_executive_window_builtin.py expectations. Tests in tests/test_executive_window_coding.py with orchestrator.service functions monkeypatched (never call real models): preview has no side effects, confirm starts exactly once, chat intent returns a confirmation not a start, run items render.

Security fix: the chat model can approve its own consequential actions. See docs/audits/2026-10-16-hr-assistant/computer-access.md ('Self-approved, a real gap') and hr-task-sweep.md gap 2. Today: MCP executive.send accepts confirm_send=true (mcp_server.py ~710, ~1102-1115), MCP browser.execute accepts approved_consequential=true (~177, ~1277), MCP executive.approve can be called by the model, and the window action executive.approve_batch is registered consequential=False (actions_executive.py ~113-120). The Executive window chat runs claude -p with every mcp__agent-os__* tool pre-allowed, so the model can approve+send in one turn.

Required: only a human click (window Confirm) can make a consequential side effect happen.
1. In mcp_server.py, when executive.send is called with confirm_send=true, or browser.execute with approved_consequential=true, or executive.approve is called: do NOT execute. Instead create a pending record with agent_os.executive.window.confirm.PendingStore().create(action_id, item, params, preview) for a matching window action and return {status:'needs_confirmation', confirm_token_issued:true, message:'Waiting for you to click Confirm in the command center.'} WITHOUT returning the token itself to the model. Preview-only calls (confirm_send false etc.) keep working unchanged. If no window action exists for that operation yet, register thin ones in actions_executive.py (consequential=True) that call the same underlying functions on confirm.
2. Mark executive.approve_batch consequential=True.
3. Make sure the pending record appears in the window's /api/pending list so the user sees it (check how server.py _previews/_pending_view read PendingStore).
4. Tests (tests/test_executive_no_self_approval.py): each of the three MCP paths with the approval flag set performs no send/execute (monkeypatch the underlying send/browser functions and assert not called), returns needs_confirmation without a token string, and leaves exactly one pending record; confirming that record through Registry.confirm performs the action once. Update existing tests that asserted the old self-approve behaviour to the new contract (do not delete coverage). Also apply the same rule to any new consequential paths in src/agent_os/executive/chat_hub.py and cloud_lane submits if they can be triggered by a model without a human Confirm.

Let the assistant answer HR policy questions ('What's our policy on overtime for drivers?') from the RTEC-HR knowledge repository with citations. See docs/audits/2026-10-16-hr-assistant/hr-task-sweep.md task 3 and gap 3. The RTEC-HR repo is a registered project (id rtec-hr-process-model resolves to the RTEC-HR checkout through agent_os.registry / agent_os.machine.resolve_path; also honour env RTEC_HR_ROOT). Its curated knowledge lives under knowledge/libraries/** as JSON claim files and Markdown (e.g. a hours-pay-benefits JSON with overtime rules and handbook page citations).
1. New module src/agent_os/executive/hr_knowledge.py: locate the RTEC-HR root; walk knowledge/** *.json and *.md, NEVER reading any path containing 'restricted-evidence', 'restricted', 'private' or files marked omitted; extract claim-like records (for JSON: objects with text/claim/statement/summary plus source/citation/page/effective/superseded fields; for Markdown: heading-delimited sections); simple keyword scoring (casefold tokens, synonym map: OT->overtime, PTO->paid time off, driver->transit driver) returning top N {text, source_path (relative), citation, effective_date, superseded_by}. Cache the parsed index in memory keyed by file mtimes. No model calls.
2. mcp_server.py: add tool hr.policy_lookup {query, limit} returning those results plus 'answer_guidance': 'Quote the claim and cite source_path/citation. If nothing relevant is found say so; do not substitute general law.'
3. Tests with a temp fake RTEC-HR tree (synthetic policy JSON + a restricted-evidence file containing a marker string that must never appear in results).

Give the command center's assistant tiered, approval-gated access to the user's computer (Windows primary, must also work on Linux for tests), per docs/audits/2026-10-16-hr-assistant/computer-access.md 'Changes' 2 and 'Security recommendation'. NO unrestricted shell for the model.
1. src/agent_os/executive/computer.py: config at ~/.agent-os/computer.json {allowed_roots: [paths], drafts_root: path} (defaults: allowed_roots = [user's Documents, Desktop, Downloads] if they exist; drafts_root = <repo>/.agent-local/executive/drafts). Path guard resolving symlinks/.. and rejecting anything outside allowed_roots. Functions: list_dir, read_text (txt/md/csv/json; .docx via python-docx if available; .xlsx via openpyxl if available; .pdf via pypdf if available; size cap 2 MB, else metadata only), search_files (name glob + optional content substring, capped), write_draft (new file under drafts_root only, never overwrite: add -vN), and consequential operations: write_file (overwrite/create under allowed_roots; makes a .bak backup first), move_file, delete_file (move to a .agent-local trash, never hard delete), open_path (os.startfile on Windows / xdg-open), run_command (argv list, no shell, cwd inside allowed_roots, timeout 120s, output capped). Every call appends a JSONL audit line (op, path, ok, timestamp; never file contents) under confirm.window_home()/computer-audit.jsonl.
2. Tiers: free = list/read/search; automatic+logged = write_draft; needs window Confirm = write_file, move_file, delete_file, open_path, run_command. Implement the Confirm tier as window actions in actions_computer.py (consequential=True; preview shows a unified diff for write_file, the exact argv for run_command, the source/target for moves) registered in builtin.py.
3. mcp_server.py tools: computer.list, computer.read, computer.search, computer.write_draft execute directly; computer.write, computer.move, computer.delete, computer.open, computer.run create a pending window confirmation (same mechanism the no-self-approval task added; never return the token to the model) and reply 'Waiting for you to click Confirm in the command center.'
4. Tests with temp allowed roots: path escape (.., absolute outside, symlink) rejected; free ops work; draft never overwrites; consequential ops do nothing until Registry.confirm; delete goes to trash; run_command refuses strings and shell metacharacters; audit has no contents.
5. Document the tiers and config in docs/orchestrator-os/executive-window.md.

Make the assistant proactive without the user having the Applicant Dashboard open. See docs/audits/2026-10-16-hr-assistant/computer-access.md 'Why nothing updates proactively' and 'Changes' 3.
1. src/agent_os/executive/watcher.py: sweep_once(): (a) pull new applicant events via agent_os.rtec_applicants applicant events + event_ack (read the existing functions; ack only after successfully publishing), publish each to the executive EventBus (agent_os.executive.event_bus) as normalized events and run executive.routing over them; (b) if any RTEC-HR knowledge file mtime changed since last sweep, record a 'knowledge_refresh_needed' event (do not run ingestion automatically); (c) write a small state file under confirm.window_home()/watcher-state.json with last sweep time, counts and errors. Read-only plus local event/index writes only: never sends, never edits Dashboard records. All sources optional: a missing Dashboard DB or RTEC-HR checkout is reported in the state, not raised.

4. The command center should show watcher health: add the state (last sweep, new applicants found, errors) to an existing provider or as one 'watcher_status' item only when there are errors or new events.
5. Tests with fake event sources: events published and acked exactly once, ack not called on publish failure, missing sources tolerated, state written.
6. Document in docs/orchestrator-os/executive-window.md.
